root_cause_label: Pixel-level heuristic matching instead of decompiling ray-tracing math
one_sentence_failure_summary: After observing vector_normalize and floating-point assembly, the agent falsely concluded the image was a simple gradient-plus-checkerboard pattern and spent 128 steps hand-tuning hardcoded pixel threshold values instead of reconstructing the underlying ray-tracing algorithm.
t_err_evidence: Based on my analysis, let me create a C program that generates the same image pattern
t_commit_evidence: At step 32 the wrong C program was created. All subsequent steps (33-160) built on this file by tweaking hardcoded thresholds rather than ever reconsidering the strategy, making failure locked in at step 32.
trigger_explanation: The agent sampled only a few pixel rows (steps 17-30) and assumed the image was composed of flat horizontal bands. The objdump output at steps 24 and 27 showed vector_normalize, fmax/fmin calls, SSE floating-point multiply/add, and a clear 2D loop over pixels with per-pixel math - all hallmarks of ray tracing - but the agent never interpreted this evidence and instead acted on the unverified assumption that visual sampling was sufficient to characterize the image generation algorithm.
